jobs.title: ASL Bilingual Specialist at The Children's Center for Communication/ Beverly School Deaf
jobs.description: Employer: The Children's Center for Communication/ Beverly School Deaf Expires: 10/31/2026 ASL Bilingual SpecialistThe Children’s Center for Communication / Beverly School for the Deaf (CCCBSD) The Children’s Center for Communication / Beverly School for the Deaf (CCCBSD) is seeking an ASL Bilingual Specialist to support the development of American Sign Language (ASL), English literacy, oracy, and functional communication skills for Deaf and hard of hearing students and to provide ASL and Deaf culture support to families and staff.This position plays an important role in supporting a bilingual, multimodal communication environment across early intervention and school-age programming. The ASL Bilingual Specialist collaborates closely with classroom teachers, speech-language pathologists, related service providers, families, and other members of the educational team.The ideal candidate brings strong ASL and English skills, knowledge of language acquisition in Deaf and hard of hearing children, and experience supporting children with developmental, physical, communication, and/or complex learning needs.Your ImpactIn this role, you will:Support the development of ASL, English literacy, oracy, and functional communication skills for Deaf and hard of hearing students.Provide professional consultation and support to teachers, therapists, and other school personnel regarding ASL and English language development.Provide families with opportunities to learn ASL and develop an understanding of Deaf culture.Collaborate with early intervention and educational teams to support communication access and language development.Provide ASL assessment and evaluation services as appropriate.Serve as a resource and mentor to staff regarding bilingual education practices for Deaf and hard of hearing students.Support the development and implementation of ASL-related IEP goals and objectives.Collaborate with teachers and speech-language pathologists on ongoing assessment of students' receptive and expressive ASL and English skills.Help staff develop ASL and English literacy materials, including classroom vocabulary, thematic language, sign/word resources, and ASL literature.Support teachers in aligning ASL instruction and vocabulary with classroom units of study.Provide consultation regarding appropriate communication strategies, accommodations, and modifications to promote student access.Collaborate with teachers and therapists on lesson planning, therapy planning, data collection, and progress monitoring related to ASL and English language development.Assist with the development, organization, and cataloging of ASL and English literacy resources.Collaborate with the Outreach Department, Reading/Literacy Specialist, and other staff to develop and facilitate ASL and English literacy opportunities for families.Participate in professional development and support training for teachers and other school personnel based on identified needs.Assist with research and evaluation of programs, resources, and practices related to ASL and English language development.Early Intervention & Family SupportThe ASL Bilingual Specialist will have opportunities to support CCCBSD's early intervention and family programming, including:Participating weekly in the Parent Infant Program.Providing ASL storytime and other ASL-rich language experiences.Consulting with families regarding ASL and Deaf culture.Participating in joint visits with early intervention providers when appropriate.Collaborating with the early intervention team on the development of Deaf Mentor opportunities.Collaborating with the ASL team on family ASL classes.Supporting families as they develop communication strategies and language opportunities at home.Evaluations & Student SupportProvide ASL evaluations for students transitioning from early intervention to school-age services.Collaborate with classroom teachers, speech-language pathologists, and other team members during three-year comprehensive reevaluations.Evaluate and document students' current ASL skills as appropriate.Provide input regarding ASL-related goals and objectives.Make recommendations regarding communication strategies, accommodations, and modifications that support student access.Maintain current knowledge of practices and assessment tools used to evaluate ASL development in Deaf and hard of hearing children.CollaborationThis position works closely with:Classroom teachersSpeech-language pathologistsRelated service providersReading/Literacy and Curriculum SpecialistsEarly intervention providersOutreach staffFamiliesOther members of the interdisciplinary teamThe ASL Bilingual Specialist serves as a resource across the organization and helps strengthen consistent, effective ASL and English language practices across programs.What We're Looking ForRequired:Bachelor's degree.Massachusetts DESE licensure in Deaf Education or eligibility for appropriate DESE licensure.Proficient ASL skills, demonstrated through a minimum Advanced Plus rating on the Sign Language Proficiency Interview (SLPI); preference given to candidates with a Superior rating.Strong English communication skills, including reading and writing.Specialized knowledge of ASL assessment and language development.Knowledge of language acquisition in Deaf and hard of hearing children.Ability to communicate effectively in both ASL and English.Ability to collaborate effectively with teachers, therapists, families, and interdisciplinary teams.Preferred experience and knowledge:Experience supporting Deaf and hard of hearing children with developmental, physical, communication, behavioral, sensory, and/or medical needs.Knowledge of Deaf culture and issues affecting Deaf and hard of hearing students.Knowledge of bilingual education approaches for Deaf and hard of hearing students.Experience with multimodal communication and AAC, or willingness to learn and collaborate in these areas.Experience developing or supporting ASL and English literacy.Experience with ASL assessment and progress monitoring.Experience providing staff consultation, mentoring, or professional development.Why Join CCCBSD?At CCCBSD, communication comes first. We believe students and staff thrive in an environment built on Humanity, Belonging, Inclusivity, Collaboration, Integrity, and Excellence.We are a Certified Kindness Workplace committed to making kindness the norm and creating a workplace where people can learn, contribute, and grow.This position offers opportunities to:Support bilingual language development for Deaf and hard of hearing students.Work collaboratively with teachers, SLPs, related service providers, early intervention providers, and families.Contribute to ASL and English literacy development across programs.Provide professional learning and mentorship to staff.Help strengthen communication access and language-rich environments for students and families.Participate in ongoing professional development and interdisciplinary collaboration.Eligible employees may also have access to benefits and programs including:15+ days of PTO annually, in addition to scheduled school breaksMedical and wellness benefitsTuition reimbursement and professional development opportunities401(k) plan with 5% employer matchPreschool discountsFree ASL classesReferral and longevity bonusesPaid Family and Medical Leave (PFML) benefitsConditions of EmploymentSuccessful candidates must complete a sign language competency assessment.Candidates must provide appropriate DESE licensure/certification or documentation of eligibility as required for the position.Employment is contingent upon successful completion of required background and employment screening.Work Environment & Physical RequirementsThis is an active school-based position. The work environment may include exposure to student behavior, personal care and hygiene needs, and other elements associated with supporting children with complex developmental and communication needs.The position may require:Moderate physical activity throughout the school day.Physically assisting or supporting students weighing up to and in excess of 50 pounds.Supporting students with mobility, positioning, transfers, or other physical needs as appropriate.Participation in community-based activities and transportation of students when applicable.Reasonable accommodations may be available to enable qualified individuals to perform the essential functions of the position.CCCBSD provides required training related to OSHA, DESE, EEC, and student and employee safety.ApplyApply directly through SchoolSpring.For questions about the position, contact Jocelyn Clark at jocelynclark@cccbsd.org.The Children’s Center for Communication / Beverly School for the Deaf is an equal opportunity employer. Deaf and hard of hearing candidates and candidates with disabilities are strongly encouraged to apply.Where Communication Comes First – Since 1876

jobs.title: Sailing Instructor - Summer Job / Seasonal Work at Lake Champlain Community Sailing Center
jobs.description: Employer: Lake Champlain Community Sailing Center Expires: 10/31/2026 Sailing InstructorOverview Would you love to share your passion for sailing with others? Do you enjoy working with youth and adults? If you answered yes, check out our Sailing Instructor position. Our team of US Sailing certified instructors spend the summer on the water providing a once in a lifetime experience to participants of all ages and abilities. Sailing instructors deliver on-the-water instruction for various classes and programs and are responsible for delivering a formal curriculum and teaching practical skills. A US Sailing Level 1 or the ability to earn one is required. Responsible to: Program Director, Program Manager Qualifications • Hold or be willing to obtain a current US Sailing Level 1 Small Boat Instructor certification at a minimum. This certification is eligible for full cost reimbursement • Up to date certifications in or willing to obtain: CPR & First Aid, CDC Concussion Training and SafeSport Training, VT State Boater’s license or out of state equivalent (available online). All certifications are eligible for full reimbursement of the costs. • Motorboat driving experience; ability to operate a motorboat in all weather conditions. • Must have a passion for sailing, the environment and experience working with kids. • Must have a positive, enthusiastic and flexible attitude. • Must possess strong problem solving skills and an ability to adapt to changing program needs depending on weather, number of students, number of boats, etc. • Must be at least 18 years of age. Pay Rate: $19.75 hourly base pay for Full Time & Part Time positions - adjusted for experience $17.75 hourly base pay for On-Call positions - adjusted for experienceResponsibilities The Sailing Instructor must be able: • Teach safety, boat handling and sailing theory to sailors of all ages in dinghies and keelboats who are beginning, intermediate or racing sailors. • Develop and implement lesson plans, new curriculum, and complete all required reports and evaluations. • Have empathy for the students and be able to adapt to their individual needs. • When scheduled, act as Race Committee during Center sponsored races. • On occasion, fulfill the duties of a Waterfront Coordinator. These duties include providing general and on shore assistance to users and Sailing Instructors, executing the rental process, and completing additional administrative work as necessary. • Enforce all policies of the Center and maintain a safe learning environment for sailors. • Complete basic environmental activities with the students throughout the week (support provided). • Help to maintain and clean the docks, boats and grounds before and after class. • Communicate with parents, sailors, and other CSC staff and users effectively and with respect. Perks: • Professional Development: All Full & Part Time instructors are eligible for full reimbursement of instructor related certifications. This includes US Sailing Level 1, CPR, Boating License, and annual US Sailing Membership. Reimbursement for US Sailing Level 2 or Level 3 must be preapproved by CSC Management. • Sailing: As an employee of Community Sailing Center you are invited to use any of our idle paddle or sail boats during business hours. • Discounts: Our organization has established relationships with local businesses to provide discounts to the Community Sailing Center Staff. You will receive a list of staff discounts at staff training. • Pro-forms: Our organization has established one or more relationships with companies willing to offer discounts on products. You will receive a list of pro-forms at staff training. Dates of Employment Applicants may apply for full-time or part-time positions for any number of the seasons listed below. Work during the spring and fall is limited – scheduling will depend heavily on the instructor’s availability and flexibility during program hours. Summer and fall employment offers the greatest opportunity for full-time work hours. Spring: April 19 – June 13 (limited hours available) Summer: June 14 – September 6 Fall: September 7 – October 11 (limited hours available)Application Instructions Apply by sending a resume and seasonal staff application (PDF available at communitysailingcenter.org/about/jobs/) to John Nagle john@communitysailingcenter.orgRecommended Application Deadline: April 15th Applications after April 15th will be accepted on a rolling basis until all positions are filled

jobs.title: 2026-2027 (NY) Academic Dean-History/Science at Achievement First
jobs.description: Employer: Achievement First Expires: 10/31/2026 School Year: 2026-2027Leading at Achievement First As an Academic Dean at Achievement First, you will be at the center of this work— coaching our teachers and driving decisions that will benefit our scholars. Here, you will be the driver of high quality coaching instruction that enables teachers to develop and deliver strong content and to help our scholars develop a lifelong love of learning. You will work with teachers to be your students’ champion who believes all students are capable of greatness. You will be a demander of excellence for yourself, your teachers and your students, an educator who helps create a vibrant school community where students have the type of powerful school experience that fosters their best and most thoughtful work. At Achievement First, you will grow as a passionate and constant leader who thrives on feedback, enjoys regular one-on-one coaching with your principal, and nurtures a voracious appetite for professional development and consistent improvement. You will cultivate schoolwide classroom cultures built on strong structures, communication and lasting relationships. Every day, you will contribute to the education of children who will go on to become the next generation of leaders in our communities. As an Academic Dean at Achievement First, your typical week would include the following, and more: Coaching and developing staff to achieve excellent student outcomes:Analyze school wide data in order to design responsive and effective student interventions.Develop highly effective instructional curriculum and schedule, in collaboration with principal and Team Teaching & Learning in the Network Support office. Observe lessons regularly and deliver targeted feedback to teachers. Collaborate with grade/subject teams to plan units, lessons and assessments; regularly share feedback. Assist teachers to devise and monitor high-impact support plans for students. Model outstanding instruction for teachers. Facilitating excellent professional development: Coordinate and manage creative, inspiring professional development sessions in line with school goals and priorities. Direct the interim assessment process to ensure teachers are using current data to drive instruction; facilitate regular, meaningful interim assessment data debriefs with teachers. Lead staff trainings at start and end of school year and on professional development day.Serve as an active member of the school leadership team: Analyze school wide data in order to design responsive student interventions.Track other useful academic data (e.g. homework completion rates); communicate progress to students, teachers and parents.Participate in regular leadership team meetings. Work closely with dean of students to support efforts in character development and positive school culture. Assist teacher leaders (e.g., coaches, grade team leaders) in developing leadership skills. Skills and Characteristics: An active and demonstrated commitment to Achievement First’s mission and values: Leading for Racial Equity, Embrace Challenge, and Go Further Together.A Track record of exemplary instructional and classroom management skills, including meeting extremely high standards for student achievement A Proven ability to proactively and effectively coach and manage adults and drive excellent student achievement through others.Superior personal organizational skills, ability to coach others to improve their organizational skills and efficiency, and ability to “zoom out” to create and manage systems and projects that require long range planning and organization.People Leadership: Strong self awareness and awareness of others, and exceptional “warm/demanding” balance when leading adults. Growth mindset for self and others; willingness to seek out feedback and ability to implement constructive feedback quickly and effectively. Mastery of and enthusiasm for subject matter. Necessary Qualifications:A bachelor’s degree; master’s degree preferred. Certified as a school leader per your state’s guidelines and requirements; If not currently certified, ability to obtain necessary state certification in specific subject and grade level is required within the first two months of employment. At least 3 years of K-12 full-time lead teaching experience with a record of high student achievement. At least 1 year of experience coaching and leading adults to obtain high student achievement. Compensation & BenefitsEmployees at Achievement First are provided with a competitive salary. Our salaries are set through a lens of equity, and based on an individual’s skills, education, and years of experience relevant to the role.Dean salaries in NY range from $94,725-$123,595.As a regular full time employee of Achievement First, you will be eligible for benefits that include medical, dental, vision, and life insurance as well as a 403(b) retirement benefit package with match and paid Family Leave.

jobs.title: Unit Leaders or Assistant Unit Leaders at Tripp Lake Camp
jobs.description: Employer: Tripp Lake Camp Expires: 10/31/2026 Tripp Lake Camp is looking for Unit Leaders!Looking to have a fantastic summer teaching your favorite activity? Well look no further!Tripp Lake Camp is located in Poland, Maine. Founded in 1911, our 7 week residential summer camp for ages 7 to 16 offers a broad array of team and individual sports, performing and visual arts, and outdoor living in a fun and stimulating environment. Our coed staff comes from all over the world to spend their summer on 260 acres with a mile of shorefront in beautiful Maine! ABOUT THE ROLEThe Advisors and Assistant Advisors are the heart of camp — equal parts mentor, manager, and nurturer. They bridge the vision of camp leadership with the day-to-day life of campers and counselors, ensuring every girl in their age group feels known, safe, and genuinely excited to beat camp. This is a role for someone who leads with warmth, thinks on her feet, and understands that the magic of camp lives in the details. CORE RESPONSIBILITIES• Oversee the daily life of your unit — from morning assembly to lights-out — ensuring smooth transitions between activities, positive culture within the group, and a nurturing environment.• Directly supervise, mentor, and evaluate a team of Bunk counselors; conduct daily check-ins and provide real-time coaching and feedback.• Know every camper in your age group by name, personality, and needs — proactively identify homesickness, social dynamics, or behavioral concerns and respond with care and intention.• Serve as the primary liaison between your age group and the broader camp leadership team; attend daily staff meetings and relay pertinent information up and down the chain.• Partner with Activity Counselors, the Health Center, and the Leadership team on conflict resolution, and camper wellbeing.• Uphold and model all camp policies including safety protocols, behavior expectations, and community values always.• Communicate thoughtfully with parents as directed — including contributing to camper notes, phone calls, or in-person conversations on visiting day.• Help coordinate and lead age group special events, and traditions that build community and belonging within your group.WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR• At least 1 year of teaching experience and/or graduate level work in teaching. experience as a counselor, or comparable leadership experience working with youth.• Natural ability to build trust with both kids and peers — warm, present, and genuinely enthusiastic about the camp experience.• Strong organizational and communication skills; able to manage multiple responsibilities simultaneously without losing sight of the individual child.• Emotional maturity and sound judgment — especially in high-pressure or sensitive situations involving campers or staff.• Experience working with or understanding of girls ages 6–16, including the social dynamics unique to all-girls environments.• First Aid and CPR certification required (or willingness to obtain prior to arrival).• A genuine love of camp — you don’t just do this job, you believe in what camp can be for a girl.COMPENSATION & BENEFITS• Salary plus room and board provided for the full duration of the summer.• Able to accomodate internships.• Travel stipend available for qualifying candidates.• Access to all camp facilities and programming on days off.• A summer that will genuinely change your life — and the lives of the girls in your age group.

Working within a specialty area, the teacher develops and implements twelve-week, age-appropriate curricula, delivers engaging, hands-on enrichment, and manages day-to-day classroom operations. ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS AND DUTIES:The essential functions or duties listed below are intended only as illustrations of the various type of work that may be performed. The omission of specific statements of duties does not exclude them from the position if the work is similar, related, or a logical assignment to the position.Provide overall program leadership and management for the assigned afterschool enrichment class, including daily transitions and classroom routines.Supervise, manage, and coach classroom assistants and assigned high school youth.Plan and implement afterschool programming for Junior Kindergarten through fifth grade, developing a high-quality, age-appropriate specialty curriculum for twelve-week sessions and delivering engaging, child-centered daily lessons that incorporate creative projects, displays, and presentations.Directly supervise children's safety; maintain a safe, positive physical, social, and emotional environment; and use social-emotional learning and trauma-informed practices to promote positive behavior and growth.Lead and participate in all program activities.Help create an environment that fosters a positive self-image, respects each child's social and cultural differences, and values each child's strengths, needs, differences, and similarities.Maintain open, friendly, and ongoing communication with families and schools regarding participant progress.Supervise participants during snack, lunch, and other program mealtimes.Record daily attendance.Participate in scheduled staff meetings and professional development.Actively engage in and support the Department's Race and Equity Initiative.Be responsible for classroom maintenance, equipment, and supplies.Document and report any out-of-the-ordinary incidents and accidents to program administrators, and during scheduled school-day hours at the same school site, as assigned.Provide classroom support under the direction of school staff by assisting classroom teachers with activities and curriculum, helping students with classwork, supporting transitions between rooms, monitoring behavior, supporting students during lunch and recess periods, maintaining open communication with school-day staff regarding participant progress, and performing general classroom support duties as needed.Perform other duties as required.Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.QUALIFICATIONSEducation/ExperienceA high school diploma or equivalent is required; some postsecondary education is preferred.Two (2) years of experience working with school-age children is required;Three (3) years of out-of-school time or enrichment experience—including curriculum planning and supervising assistants or youth workers—is preferred.Experience working with children with special needs—including implementing inclusive practices and collaborating with families and school staff—is desirable, and candidates should also demonstrate a strong interest in working with children from diverse cultural and economic backgrounds.Current First Aid and CPR (including AED) certifications are required, with training available upon hireChild Development Associate (CDA) credential; Certified Trauma-Informed Care Practitioner or comparable trauma-informed care training; Social-Emotional Learning (SEL) certification; Nurtured Heart Approach certification; Responsive Classroom training or certification; Mandated Reporter training; Special Education or Inclusion training or certification to support work with children with special needs; and an Early Childhood Education (ECE) certificate or degree preferred.Criminal Offender Record Information (CORI) and Sex Offender Registry Information (SORI), as well as a physical and TB test, are required.An equivalent combination of education, training, and experience may be considered.Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:Knowledge of child and youth development and age-appropriate pedagogy for Junior Kindergarten through fifth grade, including culturally responsive practices.Skill in designing and delivering 12-week specialty curricula with clear learning objectives, engaging activities, and differentiated supports for diverse learners.Ability to lead groups, supervise and coach classroom assistants and high school youth, and implement positive behavior support strategies to maintain a productive learning environment.Skill in communication, organization, and recordkeeping to coordinate daily operations, document progress, and collaborate effectively with families, school staff, and community partners.Ability to work and interact effectively with individuals and groups across diverse identities, cultures, backgrounds, and ideologies. SUPERVISION RECEIVED:Works under the general supervision of the Site Director, Community Schools; work is reviewed for adherence to program objectives, child safety protocols, and overall quality, while allowing considerable professional independence.SUPERVISION EXERCISED:Provides direct supervision to classroom assistants and high school youth workers; may oversee volunteers or interns assigned to the program.WORK ENVIRONMENT:Work is performed in classrooms, outdoor playgrounds, and during occasional field trips, with noise levels ranging from moderate to loudPHYSICAL DEMANDS:Occasionally, the employee may need to run during play or in response to an emergency and to lift or move a child. jobs.description: Employer: Florida Department of Children and Families Expires: 10/31/2026 Requisition No: 885691 Agency: Children and FamiliesWorking Title: CHILD PROTECTIVE INVESTIGATOR - 60071455 Pay Plan: Career ServicePosition Number: 60071455 Salary: $50,000.08 annually / $1,923.08 bi-weekly Posting Closing Date: 10/21/2026 Total Compensation Estimator ToolChild Protective Investigator Department of Children and Families Crawfordville, Florida Open CompetitiveAnticipated Vacancy This posting will be used to fill position vacancies in Career Service. Current employees will be compensated in accordance with the DCF salary policy. How you will make an impact: Be The One Who Shows Up! Children in crisis need quick action from strong, compassionate individuals dedicated to ensuring their safety. This demanding and challenging career could be your opportunity to speak for those with no voice and fight to help ensure the safety of those who cannot protect themselves. We are looking for people who are detailed-oriented, possess good decision-making skills, and can thrive in a high-pressure, fast-paced environment. When seconds count, your career decision may be the critical difference in the life of a child. What you will do: Conduct investigations of abuse, neglect, abandonment and/or special conditions for children; Collect information through observation and interviews with the children, parents, relatives, and neighbors; Assess danger threats, child vulnerabilities and caregiver protective capacities in order to determine whether a child is safe; Arrange emergency placement for any child that cannot safely remain in their home; Notify state attorney, law enforcement and child protection teams; Provide families with service linkages to agency and community resources; Conduct initial/ongoing child present and impending danger assessments; Report indication of abuse, neglect and/or abandonment to the Florida Abuse Hotline. Qualifications: A high school diploma or GED equivalent and four years of law enforcement experience or active military service (honorably discharged or status that current service reflects serving honorably); OR An associate degree or 60+ credit hours from an accredited college or university and two years of professional work experience (see examples below) or two years of law enforcement experience or active military service (honorably discharged or status that current service reflects serving honorably); Examples of professional work experience could be, although not limited to: Guardian Ad Litem or similar child advocate role Family Support Worker Group Home Worker Teacher/Teacher's Assistant/Aide Daycare Provider/Worker Therapeutic Assistant Behavioral Health Technician Family Intervention Specialist Home Health Aide/CNA Healthcare Practitioner (LPN, RN) or similar profession Nursing Facility Assistant Paramedic/EMT Firefighter Dispatcher Security/Safety Officer Emergency Management Deputy/Director or similar position Investigator (sworn/non-sworn) for a government entity Other welfare, education, first responder, emergency management or medical professional jobs that occur in high-paced, high-stress environments that require critical decision-making to occur. OR A bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university. An official letter from the college/university registrar or unofficial transcriptions with anticipated graduation dates and credits earned must be provided for all diploma/degree requirements. Proof of conferred degree such as official transcripts or copy of diploma/degree must be provided within 30 days of hire as a condition of employment. Must obtain a Florida Child Protective Investigator Certification from the Florida Certification Board within 12 months after obtaining provisional certification. All Investigators must maintain certification as a condition of employment. Information regarding certification can be found at: Florida Certification Board Valid Driver License; and Must possess operational private vehicle for use in the performance of daily work activities. Selected candidates are required to provide proof of vehicle registration and documentation of the appropriate insurance coverage within 30 days of hire as a condition of employment. The Department provides a Vehicle Insurance Allowance to assist with the cost of insurance coverage due to the use of private vehicle for work purposes. Ability to attend an 8 - 12-week mandatory training course. This training could be scheduled during day, weekend, and evening hours. Special Notes: Language proficiency may be considered in the selection process as determined by Agency needs at the time of selection. May require successful completion of pre-interview assessment or work sample to be eligible for interview. Bachelor’s or master’s degree in social work or related field preferred. Additional Information/Requirements This position will require night, weekend, and holiday work. It has also been designated as an essential position. Incumbents are expected to work during emergency situations or natural disasters and may be required to work before, during and beyond normal work hours/days. Incumbents may be exposed to possible hazardous conditions in the field. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities: Following policy and procedures, Managing Time, Assessing, Planning, Intervening, Evaluating, Documenting, Engaging, Teaming, taking appropriate actions related to Domestic Violence, Mental Health, and/or Substance Abuse, Establishing Effective Relationships with Colleagues, Professional Competencies. Must be physically able and have the ability to perform the following physical agility tasks: a.) ambulate in varied terrains to enter residences/locations as well as up and down stairs/stairwells, b.)assist with evacuation of persons served during an emergency situation, c.) have normal vision and hearing, including use of corrective devices, d.) do repetitive movements with arms, hands, neck and head, e.) bend, twist, turn, kneel, stoop, squat, push, pull, lift and walk extended distances, f.) lift and carry up to 30 pounds, g.) assist clients in and out of properties, vehicles and safety equipment/devices, h.) sit and/or stand for periods of time without a break, i.) work 16 hour shifts on occasion, j.) remain alert while on duty, k.) drive a vehicle (car or passenger van) to transport clients, during both daytime hours and nighttime hours. Candidate Profile (application) must be completed in its entirety. Include supervisor names and phone numbers for all periods of employment. Account for and explain any gaps in employment so that the hiring process is not delayed. Experience, education, training, knowledge, skills and/or abilities as well as responses to pre-qualifying questions must be verifiable to meet the minimum qualifications. It is unacceptable to use the statement “See Resume” in place of entering work history. If you experience problems applying online, please call the People First Service Center at (877) 562-7287. The State’s total compensation package for employees features a highly competitive set of employee benefits. For a more complete list of benefits, visit www.mybenefits.myflorida.com.

jobs.description: Employer: The SEED Schools Expires: 10/31/2026 School ProfileThe SEED School of Maryland is a statewide, public, college-preparatory boarding school that opened in August 2008. The school educates and boards 400 students in grades six through twelve. The SEED School is an extraordinary educational opportunity for students across the state to receive a tuition-free, college-preparatory, boarding education.The SEED School of Maryland combines a rigorous and engaging academic curriculum with life skills and enrichment activities to provide students with a thoughtfully balanced learning and living experience. Students and their families commit to a seven-year educational program that offers small class sizes, high quality teaching and learning experiences, mentoring, community service, and extracurricular activities such as sports and arts.The SEED School is centered around its character values: compassion, growth, gratitude, perseverance, integrity, respect for oneself and others, and responsibility. The SEED School staff are in partnership with parents, families, and communities to guide and support student success. The school follows a typical academic school year calendar.SEED NetworkSEED is the pioneering national network of public, college-preparatory boarding schools, offering a unique 24-hour, 5-day per week learning environment. Our tuition-free schools, the first of their kind in the U.S., are intentionally designed to serve traditionally underserved students. Supported by The SEED Foundation, we operate in Washington, D.C., Baltimore, Miami, and Los Angeles. The Foundation's College Transition & Success (CTS) team provides comprehensive support to SEED graduates from junior year through college graduation. SEED's success has gained recognition from media outlets like 60 Minutes and The New York Times, and former President Obama has lauded it as "a true success story." Learn more at www.seedfoundation.com.Position Summary:The Social Studies Teacher will provide intense academic knowledge and skills in social science, including social studies, history, American government, political science, or humanities, to secondary students utilizing course of study adopted by SEED, and other appropriate learning activities; Develops student skills of listening, speaking, reading, and writing, that are fundamental to effective communication and literate citizenship. This position reports to the Assistant Principal. Job Description:Teaches courses in social studies, history, geography, American government, political science or humanities to middle school students utilizing the course of study adopted by SEED and other appropriate curriculum publications as guidelines in teaching individual course content. Develop lesson plans to teach a balanced social studies program involving factual background material, material on current events, discussion time, and other appropriate activities designed to encourage students to develop skills and attitudes, draw conclusions, and achieve improved interpersonal relationships. Provide opportunities, when needed, for individualized and small-group instruction to adapt the curriculum to the needs of each student. Develops knowledge of the purpose, structure, and operation of the American governmental and economic system and the rights and responsibilities of American citizenship. Evaluate each student’s progress in social studies knowledge and skills. Selects and requisitions books, instructional aids, and supplies; maintains required inventory records. Supervise daily and check homework, ensure students’ academic progress, and serve as a primary point of contact for parents. Regularly assess student mastery of key skills and concepts and use this data to differentiate instruction to meet student needs. Participates in faculty committees and sponsorship of student activities. Participates cooperatively with the appropriate administrator(s) to develop the method by which he/she will be evaluated in conformance with district guidelines. Qualifications:The MS/US Social Studies will meet all qualifications and behavior standards as set by the State of Maryland authority. In accordance with certification requirements and performance expectations, all classroom teachers shall meet the following employment criteria. The minimum of a Bachelor’s Degree from an accredited college or university. A valid Maryland Teacher’s Certificate in Social Studies (6-12) or the ability to possess a conditional certificationAbility to pass a background check

jobs.title: Behavior Technician at LIFE WE DESERVE LLC
jobs.description: Employer: LIFE WE DESERVE LLC Expires: 10/31/2026 Are You Interested in the Why Behind the Behavior?You spent four years studying the brain, human development, and the laws of learning. Now, don't just read about it—apply it.At Life We Deserve, we aren't a corporate "ABA factory." We are a high-fidelity, quality-focused clinic where the science of behavior is practiced with heart. We don't just "manage" behavior; we use operant conditioning and precise shaping to give children a voice and a sense of agency. The "Aha!" Moments We Live ForWe don’t settle for "good enough." Our team works for the breakthrough moments that bridge the gap between theory and life-changing reality:Building Self-Advocacy: Moving beyond compliance to teach non-verbal learners how to say "No" and "Stop," giving them the power to advocate for their own needs.Clinical Desensitization: Using systematic shaping to transform a traumatic doctor’s visit into a tear-free, successful appointment.Cognitive Generalization: Moving a child from memorized "rote" responses to true functional literacy—reading their first words and sharing their world with others.Social Perspective Taking: Teaching the nuances of empathy and social connection, moving beyond simple labels to understanding why others feel the way they do. Why Real Clinicians Choose Life We DeserveIn-Person Mentorship (No "Zoom Supervision"): Our BCBAs are on-site and face-to-face. You get real-time, hands-on mentorship—not a face on a laptop screen.The "35-Hour Sweet Spot": We value your longevity. Full-time is 35 hours (8:30 AM – 5:00 PM), with one day a week for a late start or early exit.The "Gap-Free" Guarantee: Your paycheck is stable. If a client cancels, you still get paid. We don't believe you should be punished for a change in schedule.Elite Fieldwork Program: If you are on the BCBA track, we provide paid unrestricted hours, weekly clinical meetings, and opportunities to attend professional conferences. The Reality of the Role This is not "babysitting." It is an intensive, analytical role. To thrive here, you must:Be Analytical in the Moment: Can you remain an objective scientist when a session gets tough?Be Solution-Oriented: You will be expected to review data and read clinical articles to find ways to break down complex tasks.Value Persistence: We are the architects of our clients' progress. We don't just "pass the time"; we build competence. Who You AreThe Student: You are a Psychology grad (or senior) who wants a career, not a gig.The Observer: You understand that patience, consistency, and reinforcement are the keys to all learning—whether you've worked in childcare, research labs, or animal behavior.The Professional: You are ready to earn your RBT certification (we provide the paid training) and join a small, elite team. The PerksHealth, Dental, & Vision + 401(k).Tuition Reimbursement for those pursuing Graduate degrees (MA/MS) in related field.Paid Time Off (PTO) & Paid Training.Your Weekends are Yours: No weekend or evening sessions. Ever.

jobs.description: Employer: The SEED Schools Expires: 10/31/2026 School ProfileThe SEED School of Maryland is a statewide, public, college-preparatory boarding school that opened in August 2008. The school educates and boards 400 students in grades six through twelve. The SEED School is an extraordinary educational opportunity for students across the state to receive a tuition-free, college-preparatory, boarding education.The SEED School of Maryland combines a rigorous and engaging academic curriculum with life skills and enrichment activities to provide students with a thoughtfully balanced learning and living experience. Students and their families commit to a seven-year educational program that offers small class sizes, high quality teaching and learning experiences, mentoring, community service, and extracurricular activities such as sports and arts.The SEED School is centered around its character values: compassion, growth, gratitude, perseverance, integrity, respect for oneself and others, and responsibility. Supported by The SEED Foundation, we operate in Washington, D.C., Baltimore, Miami, and Los Angeles. The Foundation's College Transition & Success (CTS) team provides comprehensive support to SEED graduates from junior year through college graduation. SEED's success has gained recognition from media outlets like 60 Minutes and The New York Times, and former President Obama has lauded it as "a true success story." jobs.description: Employer: Concordia Language Villages Expires: 10/31/2026 Position Title:Swedish ​Language Summer Program Director or Co-director - Concordia Language Villages Position Type:SeasonalEmployment Type:Seasonal Recreation Exempt, Full-Time, TemporaryLocation:Bemidji, MinnesotaGeneral Employment Period:Five weeks in the summer (July 10-August 15)General Work Schedule (days of week):In residence in Bemidji during the summer season. January-June accounts for 20% of salary and is spent hiring summer staff and planning program for the summer.Minimum Salary:Base salary is $940/week for six weeks in residence. Salary increases possible based on education and experience. The total salary for the six weeks in-residence will be spread over the months beginning in approximately January through the end of the residential program. Virtual Village Leadership Councils will be compensated at the rate of $150 each for full attendance. Why Concordia Language Villages?For more than 60 years, Concordia Language Villages (CLV), a program of Concordia College, has brought language and culture to life through immersive experiences in the North Woods of Minnesota. Each Language Village creates a community where participants learn by living the language through conversation, food, music, activities, traditions, and everyday life.As a Summer Dean, you won’t simply work within that experience. You’ll help lead and shape it. You’ll bring together language education, cultural learning, staff leadership, and community-building to create an environment where young people can take risks, build confidence, and experience another language and culture in a meaningful way.If you’re passionate about language and culture, energized by developing others, and excited by the challenge of bringing an immersive educational community to life, CLV offers a summer leadership experience unlike most others.About the Role: The Summer Dean serves as the program director and primary leader of an individual Concordia Language Village, with overall responsibility for the leadership and operation of its summer program. You’ll oversee program development and implementation, staff leadership, budgeting, operations, and communication while ensuring the Village reflects the mission and educational philosophy of Concordia Language Villages.As a Summer Dean, you’ll be part of the broader Language Community, working alongside academic-year program leaders, participating in the Village Leadership Council, and partnering closely with your Program Director and CLV’s administrative team. This is a highly engaged leadership role that combines year-round planning and preparation with visible, hands-on leadership during the summer season.Interested in co-leading a Village? Co-dean arrangements may be considered. If applying with another person, both applicants should clearly indicate the proposed co-dean arrangement in their applications. Please note that compensation for each position is reduced in a co-dean arrangement.Please note that while the Swedish village does not share the site during their summer programming, it does share the site and facilities with the Finnish and Danish programs, which operate during the first half of the summer. As such, deans are expected to communicate professionally and proactively with their first-half counterpart(s) to ensure a smooth and successful transition. Perks of Working at CLV:Room and board provided while working on-site during the residential summer program. Build meaningful leadership experience directing an immersive language and cultural program and leading a seasonal staff team. Develop lasting professional and personal connections with educators, language professionals, and staff from a wide range of backgrounds. Make a meaningful impact by creating an environment where young people build confidence, develop language skills, and engage deeply with another culture. Grow as an educator and leader through hands-on experience in immersion education, staff development, program management, and community-building.You'll Thrive Here if You:Lead with both confidence and collaboration, providing clear direction while building strong relationships with staff, colleagues, and the broader CLV community. Stay adaptable and steady in a dynamic environment, balancing competing priorities and responding thoughtfully when plans or circumstances change. Enjoy developing others, creating a supportive environment where staff can learn, grow, and contribute their strengths. Are energized by immersive language and cultural education and committed to creating a welcoming, engaging Village experience for participants and staff.What You'll Do:Program LeadershipLead the development and implementation of a strong language and cultural program in collaboration with CLV seasonal and year-round staff.Develop and maintain a linguistically and culturally appropriate curriculum, educational program, and Village schedule, including the creation or procurement of necessary materials.Ensure the Village program operates in accordance with Concordia College and Concordia Language Villages policies and applicable Cognia and American Camp Association (ACA) standards.Gather and respond to feedback from villagers and staff, consult with CLV administrators on program needs and implementation, and promote the health, safety, and well-being of all participants.Participate in Village Leadership Councils, strategic and long-range planning, and professional development related to immersion-based language education, target language and culture, and child and youth development.Staff LeadershipServe as an active and visible leader within your Language Village, providing staff supervision and helping staff navigate conflict, CLV policies, and Village norms.Review applications; interview, hire, and onboard seasonal staff; lead Village-specific orientation; and provide ongoing staff training throughout the season.Build a collegial and productive working environment that supports staff well-being, professional development, and the mission of Concordia Language Villages.Assign and delegate staff responsibilities, conduct regular staff meetings, provide or arrange performance feedback, and coordinate disciplinary action when necessary.Serve as the primary liaison between Village staff and CLV central administration and as a primary contact for parent/guardian conversations, dismissals, discipline, and other significant participant or staff matters.Program Support & OperationsServe as a steward of your Language Village site, resources, and relationships while maintaining effective communication with CLV central administrators and staff.Monitor program and staffing expenditures and coordinate Village resources, including curricular materials, store items, foreign currency, office supplies, and other program needs.Collaborate with program, operations, facilities, health, and risk-management partners to coordinate program and support staff and address operational needs.Coordinate Village opening and closing procedures.Communication & Public Relations Communicate effectively and appropriately with participants, parents/guardians, staff, other members of the CLV community, organizational partners, and the general public on behalf of your Language Village.Represent Concordia Language Villages and its educational philosophy as requested and as a program of Concordia College.Support CLV communications and promotional efforts, including content development for publications, websites, and other initiatives.General Responsibilities of all Positions at Concordia Language VillagesClick here to view the General Responsibilities that apply to all Concordia Language Villages positionsBe familiar with and abide by specific policies set forth in the “Personnel Policies,” which are designated by Concordia Language Villages administration and individual Village deans.Read and become familiar with the responsibilities for your specific area of assignment.After receiving your Staff Handbook and other material, read all the information carefully and thoroughly before arriving at the Village.Report to orientation prior to your first session as designated by your staff agreement.Assist with setting up the Village, preparing for the next session, and maintaining the Village throughout the session.Speak the target language with villagers and staff members as much as possible.Live in community living arrangements, assigned according to gender; nearly all positions include living and sleeping in a cabin or other housing unit with villagers (participants) of the same gender; positions that do not include living with villagers do include living with other staff members of the same gender.Be prepared to use shared bathroom facilities assigned according to gender; shower and toilet stalls are private but situated within common bathroom areas shared with other staff and villagers.Model standards for behavior and be sensitive to the health and welfare of the villagers.Remain one day after your final session for cleanup, inventory, and evaluation of the program.Be at least 16 years of age to be considered for a staff position.Be at least 18 years of age to be considered for a staff position if you are not a United States citizen.Essential Functions of a Summer DeanClick here to view the complete list of Essential Functions of a Summer DeanThe essential functions of the summer dean position are listed below. Essential functions are the fundamental job duties or tasks that an employee (the dean) must be able to perform, with or without reasonable accommodation. These are statements of performance or ability necessary to fulfill the core or essential functions of the job of summer dean. These statements describe what it takes to do the job, without stipulating how. The list of essential functions is a supplement to the position description (and the position vacancy).Auditory – A dean must possess auditory ability to monitor and assess the needs of their Village program. This includes but is not limited to:Hearing and interpreting information a staff member or client is communicating verbally, in both English and the target language.Communicating over the phone in both English and the target language.Visual Acuity – A dean must possess visual ability sufficient for observation and assessment necessary to carry out the dean’s job description. This includes but is not limited to:Observing and assessing individual(s) behavior(s), especially those salient to staff and youth development.Observing and assessing program activities for their reflection of program objectives.Observing and assessing non-verbal communication signals reflective of both English and the target language.Reading and understanding printed documents in both English and the target language.Motor Function – A dean must have sufficient motor function, neuromuscular strength and coordination to effectively perform the activities required of a dean. Examples include but are not limited to:Moving from place to place within the village while carrying various objects.Attending and participating in Deans’/ Village Leadership Councils.Responding effectively in emergency situations.Communication – A dean must be able to communicate effectively and sensitively with clients, family members and staff in both English and the target language. This includes expressive and receptive modes of verbal, nonverbal and written communication. Examples include but are not limited to:Explaining Village policies and practices.Documenting assessment, action and responses of staff and clients to incidents as well as routine Village activities.Reading and assessing client, staff and program literature.Giving an accurate report of requested information to peers, parents and administration.Effectively hiring, orienting, leading, and coaching a staff team to provide the program.Emotional Health – A dean must possess the emotional health required for full use of their intellectual abilities including the ability to:Prioritize competing demands; focus and maintain attention to necessary tasks.Function in stressful circumstances; deal with the unexpected (e.g., client crisis).Separate own needs and experiences in order to maintain objectivity and a client-centered program.Adjust to changing circumstances.Handle the strong emotions of others while controlling personal responses.Behavioral – A dean must possess the ability to establish and maintain appropriate professional relationships. Factors included in this requirement are the ability to:Act ethically.Exercise sound (rational) judgment.Be compassionate.Develop mature, sensitive and effective relationships with clients, families and the CLV community.Complete all responsibilities attendant to the dean’s functional role.Interpersonal Skills – A dean must be able to effectively interact with individuals and groups respecting social and cultural diversity. This includes but is not limited to:Negotiating interpersonal conflict (conflict management skills).Directing the activity of others through communication processes.Communicating sufficiently to direct the interaction of others in written and oral forms.Influencing the actions of others.Provision of essential functions helps assure compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA).Qualifications: What We're Looking ForWe’re looking for an experienced, collaborative leader who combines strong language and cultural knowledge with the organizational skills needed to lead a complex summer program. The ideal candidate understands immersion-based language education, communicates effectively in both the Village language and English, and is comfortable leading staff, managing competing priorities, and creating an engaging environment for young people. Strong candidates will bring a commitment to the mission of Concordia Language Villages, sound judgment, and an interest in developing both programs and people. Previous leadership experience in CLV or a similar language-immersion environment is especially valuable, along with an interest in growing with the Village over multiple summers.Required Education and ExperienceIntermediate-High or higher proficiency in Swedish and English Bachelor’s degree in a related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience Minimum age of 25 (American Camp Association standard) Availability for all orientation and session dates Must possess valid work authorization for the United States Reside in the United States Preferred Education and ExperienceMaster’s degree in a related field Previous leadership position at Concordia Language Villages or in a similar, language-immersion environment Ability and willingness to make a multi-year commitment to the dean position (contingent on all parties agreeing to continuation). Returning deans reapply annually for their role.Required Skills and AbilitiesThe candidate must be able to demonstrate the following:Must be able to perform the essential functions of the Summer Dean position, with or without reasonable accommodation.Commitment to immersion-based language and cultural education. Knowledge of effective teaching strategies and methodologies for second-language learning. Excellent oral and written communication skills. Strong organizational and management skills. Commitment to the missions of Concordia College and Concordia Language Villages and to diversity, equity, and inclusion. Employment Contingencies:Background CheckDocuments Needed to Apply Required DocumentsResume/Curriculum VitaeCover LetterOptional DocumentsList of ReferencesLicensureCertificationTrainingOtherNondiscrimination StatementConcordia College does not discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment on the basis of race, color, creed, sex, religion, national origin, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, familial status, public assistance status, membership or activity in a local human rights commission, or any other legally protected status. The College is committed to providing equal opportunity in employment and fostering an inclusive and respectful environment for all. Reasonable accommodations are available to qualified individuals with disabilities throughout the recruitment process. Inquiries regarding this policy may be directed to the Office of Human Resources, Concordia College, 901 8th Street South, Moorhead, MN 56562, 218-299-3339.

We do this by building a team of mission-driven individuals, who are passionate about fostering a love of learning and creating safe, engaging experiences for children. Our vision is to bring exceptional, affordable programs to as many students, families, and schools as possible while providing a safe environment for children to explore and grow. jobs.description: Employer: Pine Island Public Schools Expires: 10/31/2026 POSITION: Full Time ADSIS Monitor Para Date Posted: September 30, 2026 Location: Pine Island High School Date Available: 2026-2027 school year Closing Date: Until FilledCompensation:Click here to view the 2026-27 Para Contract. Rates for this position can be found on p. 37This Position is Medical and/or Dental Benefit Eligible. Job Duties and Responsibilities:Independent School District #255 Pine Island is seeking a full time professional to coordinate a support room for high school students in our ADSIS program. This position works closely with the high school counselor and Special Education Director. This person must be able to work independently with students, and in small groups. Organization, communication and relationship building will be essential to being successful. This is a great opportunity for recent graduates, or someone interested in becoming a teacher Why Teach at Pine Island High School? At Pine Island, we believe that every student can succeed. Co-dean arrangements may be considered. If applying with another person, both applicants should clearly indicate the proposed co-dean arrangement in their applications. Please note that compensation for each position is reduced in a co-dean arrangement.The Italian Language Village is co-located with the Arabic Language Village. Each Village has their own housing and meal spaces, but share some staff and supplies as well as many indoor and outdoor spaces. It is important that the Italian Village Dean is prepared to collaborate with the Arabic Village Dean, and to support staff teams and villagers in sharing the site. In your cover letter, please share how you will ensure effective communication between the two Villages. Perks of Working at CLV:Room and board provided while working on-site during the residential summer program. Build meaningful leadership experience directing an immersive language and cultural program and leading a seasonal staff team. Develop lasting professional and personal connections with educators, language professionals, and staff from a wide range of backgrounds. Make a meaningful impact by creating an environment where young people build confidence, develop language skills, and engage deeply with another culture. Grow as an educator and leader through hands-on experience in immersion education, staff development, program management, and community-building.You'll Thrive Here if You:Lead with both confidence and collaboration, providing clear direction while building strong relationships with staff, colleagues, and the broader CLV community. Stay adaptable and steady in a dynamic environment, balancing competing priorities and responding thoughtfully when plans or circumstances change. Enjoy developing others, creating a supportive environment where staff can learn, grow, and contribute their strengths. Are energized by immersive language and cultural education and committed to creating a welcoming, engaging Village experience for participants and staff.What You'll Do:Program LeadershipLead the development and implementation of a strong language and cultural program in collaboration with CLV seasonal and year-round staff.Develop and maintain a linguistically and culturally appropriate curriculum, educational program, and Village schedule, including the creation or procurement of necessary materials.Ensure the Village program operates in accordance with Concordia College and Concordia Language Villages policies and applicable Cognia and American Camp Association (ACA) standards.Gather and respond to feedback from villagers and staff, consult with CLV administrators on program needs and implementation, and promote the health, safety, and well-being of all participants.Participate in Village Leadership Councils, strategic and long-range planning, and professional development related to immersion-based language education, target language and culture, and child and youth development.Staff LeadershipServe as an active and visible leader within your Language Village, providing staff supervision and helping staff navigate conflict, CLV policies, and Village norms.Review applications; interview, hire, and onboard seasonal staff; lead Village-specific orientation; and provide ongoing staff training throughout the season.Build a collegial and productive working environment that supports staff well-being, professional development, and the mission of Concordia Language Villages.Assign and delegate staff responsibilities, conduct regular staff meetings, provide or arrange performance feedback, and coordinate disciplinary action when necessary.Serve as the primary liaison between Village staff and CLV central administration and as a primary contact for parent/guardian conversations, dismissals, discipline, and other significant participant or staff matters.Program Support & OperationsServe as a steward of your Language Village site, resources, and relationships while maintaining effective communication with CLV central administrators and staff.Monitor program and staffing expenditures and coordinate Village resources, including curricular materials, store items, foreign currency, office supplies, and other program needs.Collaborate with program, operations, facilities, health, and risk-management partners to coordinate program and support staff and address operational needs.Coordinate Village opening and closing procedures.Communication & Public Relations Communicate effectively and appropriately with participants, parents/guardians, staff, other members of the CLV community, organizational partners, and the general public on behalf of your Language Village.Represent Concordia Language Villages and its educational philosophy as requested and as a program of Concordia College.Support CLV communications and promotional efforts, including content development for publications, websites, and other initiatives.General Responsibilities of all Positions at Concordia Language VillagesClick here to view the General Responsibilities that apply to all Concordia Language Villages positionsBe familiar with and abide by specific policies set forth in the “Personnel Policies,” which are designated by Concordia Language Villages administration and individual Village deans.Read and become familiar with the responsibilities for your specific area of assignment.After receiving your Staff Handbook and other material, read all the information carefully and thoroughly before arriving at the Village.Report to orientation prior to your first session as designated by your staff agreement.Assist with setting up the Village, preparing for the next session, and maintaining the Village throughout the session.Speak the target language with villagers and staff members as much as possible.Live in community living arrangements, assigned according to gender; nearly all positions include living and sleeping in a cabin or other housing unit with villagers (participants) of the same gender; positions that do not include living with villagers do include living with other staff members of the same gender.Be prepared to use shared bathroom facilities assigned according to gender; shower and toilet stalls are private but situated within common bathroom areas shared with other staff and villagers.Model standards for behavior and be sensitive to the health and welfare of the villagers.Remain one day after your final session for cleanup, inventory, and evaluation of the program.Be at least 16 years of age to be considered for a staff position.Be at least 18 years of age to be considered for a staff position if you are not a United States citizen. Essential Functions of a Summer DeanClick here to view the complete list of Essential Functions of a Summer DeanThe essential functions of the summer dean position are listed below. Essential functions are the fundamental job duties or tasks that an employee (the dean) must be able to perform, with or without reasonable accommodation. These are statements of performance or ability necessary to fulfill the core or essential functions of the job of summer dean. These statements describe what it takes to do the job, without stipulating how. The list of essential functions is a supplement to the position description (and the position vacancy).Auditory – A dean must possess auditory ability to monitor and assess the needs of their Village program. This includes but is not limited to:Hearing and interpreting information a staff member or client is communicating verbally, in both English and the target language.Communicating over the phone in both English and the target language.Visual Acuity – A dean must possess visual ability sufficient for observation and assessment necessary to carry out the dean’s job description. This includes but is not limited to:Observing and assessing individual(s) behavior(s), especially those salient to staff and youth development.Observing and assessing program activities for their reflection of program objectives.Observing and assessing non-verbal communication signals reflective of both English and the target language.Reading and understanding printed documents in both English and the target language.Motor Function – A dean must have sufficient motor function, neuromuscular strength and coordination to effectively perform the activities required of a dean. Examples include but are not limited to:Moving from place to place within the village while carrying various objects.Attending and participating in Deans’/ Village Leadership Councils.Responding effectively in emergency situations.Communication – A dean must be able to communicate effectively and sensitively with clients, family members and staff in both English and the target language. This includes expressive and receptive modes of verbal, nonverbal and written communication. Examples include but are not limited to:Explaining Village policies and practices.Documenting assessment, action and responses of staff and clients to incidents as well as routine Village activities.Reading and assessing client, staff and program literature.Giving an accurate report of requested information to peers, parents and administration.Effectively hiring, orienting, leading, and coaching a staff team to provide the program.Emotional Health – A dean must possess the emotional health required for full use of their intellectual abilities including the ability to:Prioritize competing demands; focus and maintain attention to necessary tasks.Function in stressful circumstances; deal with the unexpected (e.g., client crisis).Separate own needs and experiences in order to maintain objectivity and a client-centered program.Adjust to changing circumstances.Handle the strong emotions of others while controlling personal responses.Behavioral – A dean must possess the ability to establish and maintain appropriate professional relationships. Factors included in this requirement are the ability to:Act ethically.Exercise sound (rational) judgment.Be compassionate.Develop mature, sensitive and effective relationships with clients, families and the CLV community.Complete all responsibilities attendant to the dean’s functional role.Interpersonal Skills – A dean must be able to effectively interact with individuals and groups respecting social and cultural diversity. This includes but is not limited to:Negotiating interpersonal conflict (conflict management skills).Directing the activity of others through communication processes.Communicating sufficiently to direct the interaction of others in written and oral forms.Influencing the actions of others.Provision of essential functions helps assure compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). Qualifications: What We're Looking ForWe’re looking for an experienced, collaborative leader who combines strong language and cultural knowledge with the organizational skills needed to lead a complex summer program. The ideal candidate understands immersion-based language education, communicates effectively in both the Village language and English, and is comfortable leading staff, managing competing priorities, and creating an engaging environment for young people. Strong candidates will bring a commitment to the mission of Concordia Language Villages, sound judgment, and an interest in developing both programs and people. Knowledge of effective teaching strategies and methodologies for second-language learning. Excellent oral and written communication skills. Strong organizational and management skills. Major Responsibilities and Duties: Plans and implements curriculum and utilizes effective teaching strategies. Leadership Development Program OverviewThe Polaris Digital & Information Technology (D&IT) Leadership Development Program is a two-year rotational program designed for recent graduates interested in technology, business, and leadership. Through four six-month rotations, associates gain hands-on experience delivering digital products, developing technology solutions, and partnering with teams across Polaris to solve real business challenges. The Digital Product Development Track provides exposure to the full digital product lifecycle—from product strategy and requirements definition to software development, architecture, and solution delivery. Associates work alongside product managers, engineers, architects, and business leaders to help shape the digital products and platforms that power Polaris. This track is ideal for individuals who enjoy technology and are energized by problem-solving, collaboration, innovation, and leadership. Throughout the program, associates develop technical, business, and leadership capabilities while gaining broad exposure to how digital products and technology drive business success across Polaris. Software Engineering & Solution Development – Designing, building, testing, and enhancing digital products, applications, and platforms.Enterprise Architecture & Technology Strategy – Understanding how technology ecosystems are designed, integrated, and scaled to support business objectives. Polaris Benefit Highlights:A generous 401K employee contribution matching program.Pay for Performance Company which uniquely allows employees to receive Annual Profit-Sharing bonuses based upon the performance of the employee.Tuition Reimbursement program to support employees who want to further their education.The Selection Process:Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis throughout the fall. Selected candidates will participate in a phone screen, business screen, and virtual interview with Polaris HR and business leaders. Candidates who successfully complete the interview process may receive an offer to join the D&IT Leadership Development Program. Rotation placements are determined based on business needs, individual interests, and development goals, with start dates aligned to graduation timing in either January or June. Benefits include a lump sum payment, self-haul moving package, lease cancellation/duplicate housing reimbursement, and access to a relocation counselor. The counselor will explain available resources and assist in securing short-term housing. You will be responsible for daily transportation to and from the office. Preferred Qualifications:Previous internship, co-op, or relevant project experience.Demonstrated leadership experience through student organizations, work experiences, athletics, volunteer activities, or other involvement.Demonstrated ability to bridge technical concepts and business needs through coursework, internships, projects, or leadership experiences.Interest in digital product development, technology strategy, product management, software solutions, or technology leadership.Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively across technical and non-technical teams.Ability to think strategically and connect technology solutions to business outcomes.Demonstrated initiative, intellectual curiosity, and a passion for learning new technologies and solving complex business challenges.Strong interest in long-term career growth and development within Polaris. Collaborative Team.At GMA, you are not simply another clinician on a large corporate roster.
