jobs.title: Code Coach in Glenview Illinois at The Coder School
jobs.description: Employer: The Coder School Expires: 10/31/2026 Who We AretheCoderSchool is an after-school program for kid coders. Headquartered in Silicon Valley with locations around the country, we provide a fun, energetic, and inspirational environment to bring out that inner hacker in all kids! The future will be ever more dependent on technology so let's get our young generation ready. Learn to Code. change the World.®Job SummarytheCoderSchool is looking for passionate Code Coaches® to teach our next generation how to change the world. You'll meet incredible kids, teach them how to code, and be rewarded with an amazing experience. This is a part-time position for 2-15 hours/week (same times weekly), depending on your schedule and availability. These hours are generally sometime between 3-8pm weekdays or late morning on weekends.ResponsibilitiesA Code Coach® is a mentor who teaches kids how to code. At theCoderSchool, we have a few basic teaching styles - your assignment will depend on schedule, ability, and desire.1. Code Coaching®. Our core offering is a weekly semi-private coding session with kids. Younger kids will be taught in Scratch or Snap, while older kids gravitate towards Python/Javascript or other advanced languages like Java or C++ and beyond. The kids will generally create apps that you decide with them and may (or may not) follow our curriculum. Personalization and customization are strongly encouraged.2. Code Class. These are traditional curriculum based classes with a larger student to teacher ratio, where all students, typically ages 8-10, follow a set specific curriculum. Must be adept at handling groups of kids.This position rocks because you will:Meet, mentor, and grow amazing kids who are ready to be our next generation of coders!Meet and share with other Code Coaches® who are passionate about the latest platforms and languages, including with schools and coaches from around the country through our collaboration platformGive back to the community and help grow our next generation by sharing your knowledge of technologyHave the flexibility to teach what you're most comfortable with, and learn new things along the wayRequirementsWhat do we want from you? Read on.PASSION. All caps! This is all about the kids, we want goose bumps when your student ROCKS a code challenge.Great Communicator. There will be plenty of chatting with parents, and of course patience is a virtue when it comes to kids!Street Cred. Comp Sci degree or major is a typical, but self-learned coders are welcome to apply. Tech industry veterans with a few free hours per week are highly encouraged to apply. High school degree and up, please.Coding Skills. Strong grasp of basic procedural programming. General knowledge of a few languages is assumed - Javascript, PHP, HTML/CSS, Python, Java are most helpful. Deep technical skills aren't required - we prefer you communicate well and find answers along with students than know everything upfront.Teaching Experience. Experience teaching kids in any subject is a plus, as is experience with Scratch.Sound awesome? Shoot us an email with a cover letter and resume!

Our JROTC program is an important part of that experience, giving students another pathway to develop leadership skills and discover their strengths.We are looking for someone who understands that student success is about more than academics. The right candidate will be someone who enjoys working with young people, believes in setting high expectations, and takes pride in helping students grow into confident and responsible adults.Whether leading a classroom lesson, preparing cadets for competition, organizing a community service project, or simply encouraging a student who needs someone in their corner, this position provides countless opportunities to make a difference.Join Bemidji Area SchoolsLocated on beautiful Lake Bemidji, Bemidji offers an outstanding quality of life with abundant outdoor recreation, lakes, trails, forests, a vibrant downtown, and the amenities of a regional hub.Outdoor recreation is abundant in Bemidji. jobs.feedName: Michael D. Eisner College of Education
jobs.title: Activities Coordinator at Bemidji Area Schools
jobs.description: Employer: Bemidji Area Schools Expires: 10/31/2026 Bemidji Area Schools is seeking an experienced, strategic, and visionary 7–12 Activities Coordinator to lead one of the largest and most comprehensive activities programs in northern Minnesota.This is an exciting opportunity for an energetic and highly visible leader who believes in the power of activities to develop students, build school pride, and strengthen communities. The Activities Coordinator will provide leadership, vision, and direction for a wide range of athletic and extracurricular programs while working closely with students, coaches, advisors, families, staff, and community partners.This is a 12-month administrative position and an opportunity to play a significant role in shaping the experience of thousands of students across Bemidji Area Schools.The Bemidji CommunityLocated on the shores of beautiful Lake Bemidji, Bemidji offers an exceptional quality of life for individuals and families. Approximately 40,000 people live within the Bemidji Area Schools district boundaries, which serves approximately 4,500 students.Outdoor recreation is abundant in Bemidji. From pristine lakes and extensive bike trails to nearby state forests and year-round recreational opportunities, Bemidji offers an environment that attracts visitors from across Minnesota and beyond.Bemidji also serves as a regional hub with a vibrant downtown, locally owned shops and restaurants, major retailers, and a diverse and growing business community. It is a community large enough to provide outstanding amenities while maintaining the character and connections of a northern Minnesota community.A District Committed to Student SuccessBemidji Area Schools is proud of its strong academic reputation and commitment to student growth. The district provides students with opportunities that are difficult to find in communities of similar size, including:• A comprehensive activities and athletics program serving students across grades 7–12• Modern school facilities designed to support learning, athletics, and activities• A broad range of course offerings that provide students with opportunities to explore their interests and prepare for life after high school• Career academies designed to connect students with hands-on learning and future career opportunities• Extensive College in the High School offerings, giving students the opportunity to earn college credit while still in high schoolOur activities facilities are a point of pride. In addition to modern district competition spaces, Bemidji Area Schools partners with Bemidji State University to provide students with opportunities to compete in exceptional, collegiate-level facilities.An Opportunity to Make an ImpactThe 7–12 Activities Coordinator will be an important leader within Bemidji Area Schools and the broader Bemidji community. We are looking for someone who can combine vision and strategy with strong relationships and day-to-day leadership.The ideal candidate will be highly visible, student-centered, collaborative, organized, and committed to creating meaningful opportunities for students. This is an opportunity to lead a large and diverse activities program while helping shape the culture, traditions, and future of Bemidji Area Schools.Come lead an activities program where students have opportunities to compete, perform, discover their passions, and build relationships. Come grow with us!Position DetailsThe 7-12 Activities Coordinator has responsibility to coordinate and supervise the high school and middle school athletic and academic co-curricular program. The district is seeking candidates with the following:Effective communicator, both verbal and written.Effective motivator and organizer.Fund raising and budgeting skills.Conflict resolution and consensus building skills.Knowledge of state and federal rules and laws that apply to the co-curricular program.Secondary coaching experience.Requirements:Applicants must have secondary teaching and/or administrative experience or previous activities coordinator experience. Preference may be given to candidates who are licensed as a school administrator.Position Available:This position begins no later than December 1, 2026.Compensation:This is a 12-month position. The annual salary range for this position is $108,889 to $120,988 dependent upon qualifications and experience with a competitive fringe benefit package which includes paid vacation and sick leave, health insurance, dental insurance, 403(b) match, Health Care Savings Plan (HCSP) contribution, etc.Deadline and Application Process:To apply: www.isd31.net, select Apply Now or Careers. Please attach a cover letter, resume, three letters of recommendation, and college transcripts to the online application.Deadline: October 26, 2026If you need accommodation to complete the application or have questions, please contact Human Resources at 218-333-3100.Bemidji Area Schools is an Equal Opportunity Employer/Educator

jobs.description: Employer: Headwaters Academy Expires: 10/31/2026 Temporary Learning Center Position (Part-Time)Headwaters Academy | Bozeman, MontanaTemporary position | November 30, 2026–February 26, 2027 Headwaters Academy is a private, independent middle school in Bozeman, Montana, providing an intellectual community where curious and motivated learners connect robust academic inquiry, create lasting relationships, and embrace joyful adventure inside and outside the classroom.Position OverviewHeadwaters Academy seeks a flexible, student-centered educator to join our Learning Center team during a maternity leave.The primary focus of this position is supporting students and teachers through the Learning Center. Shared School ResponsibilitiesSupervise assigned lunch periods.Support afternoon pickup and dismissal.Provide front desk coverage following established school procedures.Provide student supervision or coverage as needed.Participate in other shared duties appropriate to the position and schedule.Contribute to a warm, collaborative, and student-centered middle school community.QualificationsWorking towards Education degree or Bachelor’s degree requiredExperience working with middle school students preferred.Experience in education, academic support, tutoring, student support, or a related field preferred.Strong communication, organization, and collaboration skills.Ability to support students both individually and within classroom settings. jobs.feedName: Michael D. Eisner College of Education
jobs.title: Outdoor Trip Leader at Overland Summers
jobs.description: Employer: Overland Summers Expires: 10/31/2026 Each summer, we offer six weeks of hiking, language, and service trips across the country and around the world. We hire students and recent graduates to lead these outdoors programs. Whether you’re summiting peaks in the Rockies, kayaking through fjords in Norway,, or restoring trails in Alaska, the goal for our leaders is the same: catalyze in students an understanding of the world beyond themselves, beyond their own needs and wants, and inspire them to come together as a team. What is an Overland summer like?There are three parts to an Overland summer: training, leading and closing. The Overland summer begins in early June with Leader Training in Williamstown, Massachusetts. The entire staff camps and shares all meals through two weeks of seminars, hands-on workshops and a multi-day hiking trip. Leader Training is a time to sharpen leadership skills, master the details of trip logistics, and build effective working relationships with co-leaders and the full-time staff. Overland leaders co-lead a trip or a series of trips with one or two other leaders. For six weeks, leaders are responsible for maintaining the health and well-being of their students, managing day-to-day logistics, transporting students in a 15-passenger van (on some trips towing a utility trailer), working within a budget, planning and organizing meals, completing required paperwork, communicating with the Overland office and photographing the experience. Leaders manage risks in the field and serve as a positive role model to students, working to bring every member of the group together as a team. The Overland summer ends the first week of August with Leader Closing in Williamstown, during which leaders reconnect with the rest of the staff, debrief their leading experience, and follow up with their students via written communications. How to ApplyThe application process consists of a written application and resume, three references, and two rounds of interviews. Our Leader Hiring team aims to find a good fit between an applicant and a trip, as well as between co-leaders. We invite you to apply and look forward to getting to know you. Here is the link to our 2027 Application! Application DeadlinesOverland has three application deadlines over the course of the year:Sunday, November 29th, 2026Sunday, January 31st, 2027Sunday, March 28th, 2027We assess applications on a rolling basis and make offers beginning in October until all positions are filled. If you’re excited about leading for Overland this summer, we recommend you apply early! Minimum Requirements & ExpectationsPassion for working with kids in an outdoor environmentA valid driver’s license (while the majority of our trips require leaders to have had a valid driver’s license for at least 2 years, a select few trips do not have this requirement)The ability to lift and carry 40 lbs or more of gear or equipmentThe ability to pass a swimming test and lifeguard certification course (offered at training)CPR/AED and Wilderness First Aid certifications valid through August, 2027 (not necessary at time of applying, and Overland can help reimburse leaders for these certifications)A clean driving record, a positive local police check, CORI, SORI, and three written referencesA recent physical indicating excellent physical and mental healthSome (but not all!) trips require specialized hiking and camping skills, bicycling experience, or foreign language skills Dates of EmploymentOur leaders arrive in Williamstown, Massachusetts on June 13th, 2027 for Leader Training. At the end of the summer, the entire staff returns to Williamstown for Leader Closing. Leaders depart August 9th. Leader CompensationSalaries for first year leaders range from $2,750 to $3,250 based on previous experience and the leader’s role and responsibilities at Overland. In addition, Overland pays:50% of the leader’s travel expenses to-and-from Williamstown (up to $250)—Overland also organizes shuttles from Boston and Albany airports, or carpools from other locations (when possible)WFA & CPR expenses (up to $350)And, of course, all trip expenses while leading are provided: all flights, accommodations, meals, and activities (for example, rafting, kayaking, ice climbing, etc.). In the field between trips, leaders receive two nights of hotel accommodations and all meals.

jobs.description: Employer: Seneca Family of Agencies Expires: 10/31/2026 If you're driven by compassion and committed to making a meaningful difference, we invite you to join our team as a Bilingual Lead Care Manager!As a Bilingual Lead Care Manager, you'll be a trusted guide and advocate, serving as the central support for youth and families seeking care coordination and community connections. jobs.description: Employer: The Meridian School Expires: 10/31/2026 DescriptionAre you...A curious and creative teacher excited to bridge intellect, heart, and imagination in the classroom?A compassionate educator and role model for students?An enthusiastic community member eager to collaborate and build relationships?A teacher who loves project-based learning? Then read on!Ideal candidates possess a background in pre-Kindergarten and/or early childhood education, previous experience working with diverse learners, and experience supporting students in the classroom or in an afterschool setting.Who We Are:We are an independent PreK-5 school located in Wallingford's Good Shepherd Center. Meridian inspires children to approach learning with passion and curiosity. Classes are small, and our curriculum is challenging. We encourage students to be reflective and to explore a diversity of thoughts and perspectives. We ask a lot of our students. We ask them to try, to make mistakes, to rebound, to apologize, to move forward with integrity. We ask them to take intellectual risks, and to be thoughtful, caring community members. As citizens of the world, we encourage them to make connections between themselves, their local community, and the larger global society. We strive for Meridian students to develop into curious, compassionate, responsible young adolescents who begin to understand the power that resides in their hearts and their minds.We believe the challenges of our world require culturally competent, well-rounded, critically thinking individuals prepared to be responsible and active global citizens. This is our work as educators in partnership with students and their families. We offer an academic education that balances children's intellectual, emotional, and social growth. We believe an inclusive, diverse school community promotes a child’s sense of belonging.
